2.text: Comets are called “smoking-stars” by the Chukchee. The word “smoke”

3.text: indicates that they suppose much cooking is being done there. Planets are

4.text: called “crooked-way stars,” because of their irregular path. Among these,

5.text: Venus has a separate name, Hɪtoˊ-Lap. The first part of this name means
5.resolved: Hɪto' = H + ɪ(U+026A) + t + o + ˊ(U+02CA); Lap = L + a + p, ordinary capitalized word, not small-cap

9.text: means literally “one looking on.” The Chukchee name of Venus, therefore,

23.text: are but little more than names. These names may replace one another.

24.text: The first name is used chiefly in cosmogonical tales; the second, and more

25.text: particularly the third, in prayers and incantations.

26.text: All of these “Beings” are powerful, and just and benevolent toward man.

27.text: They represent a very loose and indefinite personification of the creative

28.text: principle of the world, and are similar to Great Manitou or to Wakanda of

29.text: the Indians, which are quite as indefinite in meaning. The Zenith, the Mid-

30.text: day, the Dawn, are also often considered identical with the Creator of the

31.text: world. With those who have been baptized, the Christian God, under the

32.text: name of Eˊñeñ,³ has taken a place side by side with these vague superior
32.note: handle {E'n~en~} = Eˊñeñ, confirmed at 4x; superscript footnote marker 3 (U+00B3) also confirmed
32.as_typed: name of {E'n~en~},³ has taken a place side by side with these vague superior

33.text: beings. The Chukchee, however, point out that the Creator does not belong

34.text: to those sacrificed to. They say there is no need to sacrifice to the Creator.

35.text: Upper Being, Merciful Being, Life-giving Being, Luck-giving Being, may receive

36.text: sacrifices, though these sacrifices are not included in the yearly cycle of cere-

37.text: monials. More often sacrifices to Dawn, Zenith, and Mid-day are at the same

38.text: time offered to the benevolent “Beings” mentioned before.
